title: Massachusetts Schools
scope: This ledger ranks states on NCES NPEFS current expenditures per pupil for fiscal year 2024 (school year 2023-24), reports Massachusetts Fall 2024 public K-12 enrollment, DESE / E2C 2025-26 enrollment by grade, race, and selected populations (low income, English learners, high needs, students with disabilities), DESE Chapter 74 career technical education enrollment for 2025-26, Next Generation MCAS 2025 meeting-or-exceeding shares, 2024-25 attendance and dropout rates, and DESE district total expenditures per pupil for FY 2025.
exclusions: Does not cover national NAEP, higher education, charter-only national files, waitlists, lottery outcomes, or advice about a school choice. Waitlists and lottery outcomes are not a published statewide table.
heritage: Formerly Education Fast Facts, Enrollment by Grade, MCAS NEXTGEN, School Attendance, Dropouts & Graduates, MA Demographics, and School Finances
vintage_note: Rebuilt Aug 15, 2026 from NCES NPEFS FY 2024 (stfis24_1a; current expenditures TE5 over membership MEMBR23). U.S. $17,644 and Massachusetts $27,008 match First Look 2026-008 Table 4. Fall 2024 enrollment is Digest 2025 table 203.20 (U.S. 49,387,403). Later views compiled Aug 15, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary. Tableau companions compiled Aug 16, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary.

q: Enrollment by grade, demographics, MCAS, attendance, dropouts, school finances, and Chapter 74 vocational-technical programs for Massachusetts districts.
lead: Current expenditures per public-school pupil were $17,644 in the United States in fiscal year 2024 (SRC-606-01). Massachusetts spent $27,008, rank 5 of 51 (derived, SRC-606-01). Fall 2024 enrollment in Massachusetts was 915,932 (SRC-606-02). Chapter 74 career technical education enrolled 59,962 Massachusetts high-school students in 2025-26, 21.2 percent of high-school enrollment (SRC-606-03). That is 5,676 more students than in 2021-22 (derived, SRC-606-03). 95 districts and 111 schools reported a Chapter 74 program; 29 were regional vocational or agricultural districts (derived, SRC-606-03). Greater Lowell Regional Vocational Technical was the largest district at 2,312 (SRC-606-03). Grade-9 exploratory enrolled 17,147; the largest occupational program was Health Assisting at 3,617 (SRC-606-03). After Dark partnership enrollment was 406, a published subset of Chapter 74 (SRC-606-03). All college-and-career pathways together enrolled 82,903 (SRC-606-03). On the 2025 Next Generation MCAS, 42.0% of grades 3-8 students met or exceeded expectations in English language arts and 41.0% in mathematics (SRC-606-04). Grade 10 was 51.0% ELA and 45.0% math (SRC-606-04). The attendance rate was 93.2% in 2024-25; 18.8% of students were chronically absent (SRC-606-05). The high-school dropout rate was 1.8%, 5,143 students (SRC-606-06). Among districts, Truro had the highest total expenditures per pupil at $59,111 (SRC-606-07). Waitlists and lottery outcomes are not a published statewide table. In 2025-26, 41.1% of Massachusetts public-school students were low income and 13.4% were English learners (SRC-606-08). Kindergarten enrolled 60,871 students (SRC-606-08).
